Section 75(1) of the Bank of South Sudan Act 2011 names the Auditor General as the auditor of the Bank's accounts and records, which 'shall be audited annually in accordance with International Standards on Auditing'; Section 76(1) refers to statements certified by 'the Auditor General and the Bank's external auditors', and Section 24(3)(h) has the Audit Committee recommend appointment of an external audit firm, but no firm is named in the Act. A February 2023 Bank of South Sudan notice shows the Auditor General inviting private firms to bid for the external audit of the Bank's statements for 2022 and 2023 without naming a winner.

Article 48(5) of the Central Bank of Iraq Law (Coalition Provisional Authority Order No. 56, 2004) provides that 'The CBI shall be subject to audit by the Board of Supreme Audit.' Article 48(1)-(2) separately requires the financial statements to be audited at least annually by an external audit firm experienced in auditing central banks, appointed each year by the Minister of Finance and limited to five cumulative years, but the law names no firm; the Central Bank of Iraq's published financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2005 carry an auditor's report dated 1 October 2006 in Baghdad with no firm name in the extracted text.
source_title: Coalition Provisional Authority Order Number 56 - Central Bank Law (Iraq National Investment Commission)
